headline_seed: Three dead and several injured in shooting at food festival near Seattle's Space Needle - BBC

consensus_facts: A shooting occurred at the Bite of Seattle food festival at Seattle Center, near the Space Needle, on Sunday, July 26, 2026.
The shooting happened at approximately 6 p.m. local time.
Three people were killed and four others were injured.
Two individuals died at the scene and a third died at a hospital.
The injured included a toddler / a young boy.
The three people killed were identified by police as a 19-year-old man, a 44-year-old man, and a 56-year-old woman.
Police believe two suspects were shooting at each other.
One suspect was taken into custody and a second suspect was at large / being sought.
Assistant/Acting Seattle Police Chief Tyrone Davis said there was no ongoing threat to the public.
The suspect in custody was described as a 'young person' who was being questioned.
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson called the shooting an 'act of horrific violence' and said no one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event.
The Bite of Seattle is an annual three-day festival, with Sunday being its final day, and it draws roughly 350,000 attendees.
Witnesses described panicked, chaotic scenes with people running for cover, and some initially mistook the gunfire for fireworks.

disagreements.topic: Number of people shot vs. killed/wounded total

positions.NBC News: States seven people were shot at the complex; three died and four were injured, plus notes a fifth person (40-year-old woman) with minor injuries declined hospital transport.
positions.BBC News: Reports three dead and four injured taken to hospital in stable condition, 'while a fifth chose not to' go to hospital.
positions.Los Angeles Times: Reports three killed and four wounded; notes two festival attendees told KOMO they heard 'seven to eight shots.'
positions.ABC News: Reports three killed and four injured, one of whom (40-year-old woman) declined hospital transport.

disagreements.topic: Whether a victim died at the hospital after being transported

positions.NBC News: States four injured, including a toddler, were taken to Harborview Medical Center 'where one of them died,' seemingly conflating the third death with a transported patient.
positions.Los Angeles Times: States two victims were pronounced dead at the scene and a third died at a hospital, with four hospitalized in stable condition.
positions.BBC News: States two deaths confirmed at scene and one person died later in hospital, with four injured in stable condition.

disagreements.topic: Number of suspects arrested (initial vs. corrected)

positions.BBC News: Notes Mayor Wilson originally announced two suspects had been taken into custody before updating her statement to one suspect in custody with the other at large.
positions.Los Angeles Times: Reports one suspect arrested, one on the loose; does not mention the initial two-in-custody statement.
positions.NBC News: Reports one gunman surrendered/was taken into custody, one fled.
positions.ABC News: Reports one suspect in custody, one at large.

positions.NBC News: Specifies a pediatric male patient, a 23-year-old male, and a 39-year-old female in satisfactory condition, plus a 40-year-old woman who declined transport, citing hospital and fire spokespeople.
positions.ABC News: Lists injured as a boy, a 23-year-old man, and a 39-year-old woman in stable condition, plus a 40-year-old woman with minor injuries who declined the hospital.
positions.Los Angeles Times / BBC News: Refer more generally to four injured including a 2-year-old boy in stable condition without the full breakdown of ages.

framing_analysis.Associated Press: Two of the three AP items (Articles 1 and 6) are essentially photo galleries with brief captions and a short lede; Article 4 is a video-driven brief. AP leads with the tourist-landmark framing ('beneath Seattle's Space Needle'), sticks to police-attributed facts, and emphasizes the search for the second suspect. Neutral wire phrasing throughout; minimal witness color and no policy context.
framing_analysis.Los Angeles Times: Leads with the casualty count and specifically foregrounds the toddler in the headline. Gives heavy weight to witness testimony (Wakonabo, Carris, Mohammed) and the panicked scene. Notably closes with national gun-violence context — 270 mass shootings this year per Gun Violence Archive and a downward violent-crime trend — plus a 'More to Read' list of other festival shootings, situating the event within a broader gun-violence pattern.
framing_analysis.BBC News: International framing centered on the iconic Space Needle tourist spot. Emphasizes the 'horrible' and 'chaotic' witness scene and is the outlet most careful about correcting the record, explicitly noting the mayor first said two were in custody then revised it. Foregrounds political condemnation (Wilson, Gov. Ferguson, Rep. Jayapal) and the flag lowered to half-mast. Adds sidebar links to unrelated shootings.
framing_analysis.NBC News: Frames the event squarely as a 'shootout' between two gunmen in both headline and body. Most granular on the medical details — cites Harborview trauma center, hospital spokesperson Susan Gregg, and fire spokesperson Grace Nuñez with specific victim conditions. Emphasizes that police did not discharge their weapons and that two guns were recovered. Includes the most vivid witness quotes ('There's bodies everywhere... I counted eight') and adds ATF involvement and historical Seattle Center/World's Fair context.
framing_analysis.ABC News: Compact report leading with the 'Horrific violence' mayoral quote. Emphasizes rapid police response ('within seconds') and the emergency aid officers rendered. Provides the victim age/gender breakdown for both killed and injured. Leans on official statements from Davis and Wilson with relatively little independent witness reporting or broader context.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources (police reports, court filings, official transcripts, press releases) were located for this story. All facts derive from news reports citing a Sunday-night police news conference and official statements, so no independent document-level verification is possible.

Multiple outlets (LA Times, ABC, NBC) attribute core facts to the same Assistant/Acting Police Chief Tyrone Davis news conference and Mayor Katie Wilson statement, meaning much of the apparent corroboration traces back to a shared set of official sources rather than independent reporting.
missing_context: No outlet reports a motive or the relationship between the two suspects, beyond the police belief that they were shooting at each other.
The identity, age, or any description of either suspect (beyond 'a young person' for the one in custody) is not provided; police said they had no description of the outstanding suspect.
No outlet clarifies whether any of the three deceased or the injured were the suspects themselves or purely bystanders.
There is an unresolved discrepancy between reports of four injured (most outlets) and NBC's reference to seven people shot, which no outlet fully reconciles.
No update is given on whether the second suspect was ultimately apprehended, as all reports reflect the immediate aftermath.
No outlet describes the festival's security posture or whether any screening/weapons policy was in place at Seattle Center.

The LA Times is the only outlet to place the shooting in national gun-violence statistical context; the wire and other outlets omit this framing entirely, and none link the number to comparable event contexts beyond sidebar headlines.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Five distinct outlets covered the same event with materially different emphasis — from AP's spare wire captions to NBC's 'shootout' framing and detailed medical breakdown, to the LA Times' national gun-violence contextualization — and there are unreconciled discrepancies (four injured vs. seven shot, initial two-in-custody claim) worth surfacing, making this a coverage-report rather than a straight REPORT.
